# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**RE: Appeal of Denial – Reference #POC-1C51E72E1E-65750**
**Member:** Skyler Ellison
**Member ID:** W240749705
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-24
**Requested Service:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
**Governing Policy:** Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery (effective 2025-11-15, updated 2026-01-01) — https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/spine-surgery-2025-11-15-updated-2026-01-01/

Dear PacificSource Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for lower back disc surgery/decompression (CPT 63030), which was denied on 2026-08-24 for "incomplete documentation." My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking PacificSource to reconsider this decision using the plan's own Spine Surgery guideline and the records already in my file.

## Why I believe the denial should be reversed

The denial states that the documentation submitted does not allow a determination of medical necessity. I have reviewed the guideline that PacificSource applied, and I believe the records already submitted address the specific requirements it lists.

**1. Physical therapy and complementary conservative treatment**

The guideline states:

> "Conservative management 1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

My records show I completed supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, over a 10-week course from 2026-04-24 to 2026-07-03, totaling 24 visits, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. In addition to physical therapy, I also received:

> "Anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics 2 Adjunctive medications such as nerve membrane stabilizers or muscle relaxants 2 Epidural corticosteroid injection(s) 2 Alternative therapies such as acupuncture, chiropractic manipulation, massage therapy, activity modification, and/or a trial period of rest (e.g., from the aggravating/contributing factors), where applicable"

Specifically, I used NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and I received an epidural corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-30, which gave approximately 3 weeks of partial relief. This appears to satisfy both the physical therapy requirement and the "at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy" requirement.

**2. Documented, patient-specific program with compliance**

The guideline further requires:

> "Participation in a patient-specific or tailored program Initial active instruction by MD/DO/PT with redemonstration of patient ability to perform exercises Compliance (documented or by clinician attestation on follow-up evaluation)"

My physical therapy discharge note documents a tailored 10-week, 24-visit program specific to my condition, which I completed in full.

**3. Failure of conservative management**

The guideline states that failure of conservative management requires:

> "Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation More invasive forms of therapy are being considered Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

I completed the full course of physical therapy, medication management, and injection therapy described above for this episode of low back pain, which has now lasted 12 months. Despite this, I continue to have significant limitations: I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes, and I have ongoing radicular pain into my right calf. My surgeon is now considering surgery as the next, more invasive step because these conservative measures did not resolve my symptoms.

**4. Imaging and neurologic findings**

My MRI of the lumbar spine, dated 2026-07-28, shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. My exam findings include positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to this imaged level. The guideline notes:

> "The requirement for a period of conservative management as a prerequisite to a surgical procedure is waived when there is evidence of progressive nerve or spinal cord compression resulting in a significant neurologic deficit, or when myelopathy, weakness, or bladder disturbance is present."

I want to be clear that I did complete a full course of conservative management as described above; I am including this provision because my records also document a neurologic deficit at the corresponding level, which I believe is directly relevant to the medical necessity of surgery at this time.

**5. Symptom severity and functional impact**

The guideline states:

> "For purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform at least two (2) ADLs and/or IADLs."

My records document that I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes and that I have radicular pain into my right calf. [Pain intensity has not been recorded on a numeric 0–10 scale in the records provided to me; if this is needed, I am asking my surgeon's office to supply that documentation.] I am also asking PacificSource to confirm what additional ADL/IADL documentation, if any, is needed to complete this part of the review.

**6. Clinical reevaluation timing**

The guideline requires that:

> "Clinical reevaluation must be done in reasonable proximity to the anticipated date of service such that the patient's condition would be unlikely to change by the date of service."

My most recent imaging and clinical evaluation were completed on 2026-07-28, close to the time this surgery was requested. If PacificSource requires a more recent reevaluation to confirm my condition has not changed, I am willing to obtain one, and I ask that the plan specify exactly what is missing so my surgeon's office can provide it promptly.

## What I am asking

I am asking PacificSource to reconsider and approve authorization for CPT 63030 based on the records already submitted, which I believe address the conservative management, complementary treatment, and clinical findings described in the plan's own Spine Surgery guideline. If any specific document is still considered missing, I respectfully ask that PacificSource identify exactly what is needed so my surgeon's office and I can supply it without delay.

I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-02-20**, and I am submitting it well within that window.

I understand that this letter is a request for reconsideration and does not by itself guarantee that coverage will be approved.

Thank you for reviewing my appeal.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Skyler Ellison
Member ID: W240749705
Date: [date of signature]
Phone: [phone number]
Email: [email address]
